# Run ledger — P26.12 (federal surveillance legislation via Congress.gov)

## Spec / Base / Branch / Config

- **Spec:** `docs/tickets/P26.12__congress-legislation.md` (SOURCES.11,
  manifest row 109) — the federal companion to the P26.11 state sweep:
  a bounded, keyword-filtered Congress.gov v3 bill-index sweep emitting
  typed, evidence-backed claims (title / status / chamber / congress /
  matched keyword) for surveillance-relevant federal bills and
  resolutions — proposed legislation as live claims, **never** a §11.14
  `LegalInstrument`.
- **Branch:** `devin/p26-12-congress-legislation` — stacked on
  `devin/p26-11-next-sources` (PR #103). Head at hosted run: `ecd1cac`.
- **Date:** 2026-09-18. Same GCP posture as P26.8–P26.11: user account
  `14stevevitali@gmail.com` on `zeta-medley-508121-u7`; per-job upserts
  (`gcloud run jobs deploy`), never `scheduled-ops.sh --apply`. Local Docker

## Recon findings (live, 2026-09-18 — keyed `X-Api-Key` probes)

| surface | verdict |
|---|---|
| auth | **`X-Api-Key` header → 200** (verified); keyless → 403 `{"error":{"code":"API_KEY_MISSING",…}}` — a recorded challenge, never defeated. The existing `sig-data-gov-key` (api.data.gov) covers api.congress.gov — no new credential |
| congress scoping | **path-based** — `/v3/bill/{congress}` (the `congress` query param on `/v3/bill` is ignored: returns all ~430k records); `/v3/bill/119` → `pagination.count = 18,887` |
| paging | `limit ∈ [1,250]` (documented max — the API clamps >250); `pagination` carries `count` + `next` (offset-based) |
| `sort=updateDate+desc` | documented but **observed non-functional** on the bill list (asc/desc byte-identical) — recorded in the plan; no result depends on list order |
| `fromDateTime`/`toDateTime` | accepted (updateDate window) — not used; the sweep takes the full bounded index so verbatim local matching sees every bill |
| keyword query | **none** on the bill list — matching is LOCAL against `legislation_vocab.toml` (the P26.11 verbatim match-of-record rule) |
| quota | documented **5,000 requests/hour** (api.congress.gov README); observed `x-ratelimit-limit: 20000` / remaining ≈19986 on the staged key. The ~77-request sweep is trivially inside the window |
| error envelope | `{"error":{"code","message"}}` — api.data.gov shape → `ContentDrift`, fail closed |
| later pages | one scan probe past page 1 answered **HTTP 403** during recon — recorded, not re-probed (the D-SOURCES.10-1 lesson); the hosted sweep itself ran clean (76 pages, 0 refusals) |

## What landed

### 1. The reviewed sweep plan — `congress_gov_plan.toml` (new, versioned `2026.09.18`)

All bounds DATA, never code (SIG-ENG-001): `congresses = [119]` (the current
session — a congress that ENDS stops generating proposed instruments and its
claims are already recorded, append-only), `endpoint = "/bill"`,
`per_page = 250` (the verified v3 bound), `sort = "updateDate+desc"` (sent for
the record, observed non-functional), and `max_pages_per_congress = 96` — the
hard bound that truncates loud (a count beyond 24,000 bills records
`truncated` on every page's outcome row; the sweep never crawls past it).
Every live-verified finding above is recorded in the plan header.

### 2. The vocabulary — `legislation_vocab.toml` → `2026.09.18.2`

Two federal additions to the shared P26.11 set: **`fisa_702`** (`foreign
intelligence surveillance`, `\bfisa\b`, `section 702`, `title vii of the
foreign intelligence`, `702 reauthorization`) and **`government_surveillance`**
(government/mass/warrantless surveillance, surveillance reform/transparency/
accountability/state). Every ticket-named federal phrase is covered; the
shared terms (geofence, stingray/cell-site simulator, data broker, ALPR,
facial recognition, drone, body-worn camera, ShotSpotter, RTCC, predictive
policing) apply unchanged — both files are shared with the OpenStates path.

### 3. The source registration + rights — `sources.toml`, flipped GL-GATE-06

`congress_gov` registered (186 → 187) and **flipped** (`ingestion_permitted`,
65 → 66 loadable) under the same GL-GATE-06 delegated pattern: Congress.gov
bill/resolution metadata is a US federal government work → public domain
(17 U.S.C. §105) → `CC0-1.0`, and the API's documented purpose is verbatim
"view, retrieve, and re-use machine-readable data" (api.congress.gov README,
retrieved 2026-09-18). Packet: `docs/build/reports/rights/congress_gov.md`
(verbatim terms quoted, LOW counsel flag). The api.data.gov key is auth, not
the rights basis (HG-09).

### 4. Connector — `accountability.py` (the federal layer of the P26.11 path)

- `congress_gov_config()` / `congress_gov_plan()` accessors; `congress_gov`
  added to the vocab's source-id map and the predicate allowlist
  (`+bill_chamber` — the federal chamber-of-origin a state bill does not
  surface); `vocab_version 2026.09.18.2`.
- `fetch`: keyed `X-Api-Key` header for every congress_gov target — the key
  resolves from `$SIG_DATA_GOV_KEY` only, **never** the URL, so no credential
  lands in source_uri / run rows (HG-09, the P26.4 transport rule).
  Keyless → the upstream 403 stands as a recorded challenge.
- `parse`/`extract` fail closed: `congress_gov_bills` kind; a `{"error":…}`
  envelope, malformed JSON, or a non-`bills` payload is `ContentDrift`, never
  a fabricated bill. An empty `bills` list is an honest empty page.
- `discover_more`: the captured seed page IS the discovery surface — each
  seed's `pagination.count` names its congress index size and expands the
  remaining `/bill/{congress}?offset=N` pages (numeric offset order,
  per-congress bound, deduped by URL, one bounded pass — a generated page
  never re-expands). Congress + page offset + per_page + plan_version ride
  the target row as data; `ctx.resolved_targets` carries provenance to the
  children's post-capture stages.
- `normalize` — the claim-shape map on the record's own title (local
  verbatim scan = match of record): a matched bill emits a `legislative_bill`
  entity row + `bill_external_id` (`{congress}-{type}-{number}`),
  `bill_identifier` (conventional citation `S. 1355` typed / verbatim
  `S 1355` raw — the reviewed `type_prefixes` map; unmapped type falls back
  verbatim), `bill_title`, `bill_session` (the congress number),
  `bill_jurisdiction` (the reviewed `United States Congress` constant),
  `bill_chamber` (verbatim `originChamber`), `bill_status` +
  `bill_status_date` (the record's own `latestAction` verbatim), and one
  `bill_matched_keyword` per typed term carrying the **verbatim** literal as
  `raw_value` with a byte-range-into-title locator. Evidence carries the
  derived congress.gov public record URL (`type_slugs` map →
  `/bill/{ordinal}-congress/{slug}/{number}`; unmapped type falls back to
  the record's verbatim API url) + a `Locator.row` into the captured page.
  Unmatched bills keep the `index_only` `primary_record` evidence link —
  recorded metadata only, never a fact. A federal bill is **PROPOSED law** —
  no enactment is inferred from any field (§3.1).
- Per-page `bill_query` non-claim outcome rows (congress, page_offset,
  outcome, counts, `truncated` when `pagination.count` exceeds the page,
  plan_version, legislation vocab version) serialize onto the fetch
  record's `document_outcomes` (runner.py forwards the two new fields).
- Claims carry **no volatile field** — no `observed_at`, no retrieval
  timestamp, no capture id keys a claim (SIG-INGEST-003/017). Claim identity
  is stable bill content → an unchanged record digests identically on ANY
  re-run; the observation time lives on capture/evidence.

### 5. Wiring — live_targets, allowlist, cadence, runner

`live_targets.toml`: the congress-scoped seed page
(`congress-gov-bill-119-p1`, `rate_limit_per_min = 30` — the reviewed
budget, far inside 5,000/hour). `api_allowlist.toml`: `api.congress.gov`
`/v3` row. `ops/cadence.toml`: `sig-ingest-congress-gov` monthly
(`0 5 3 * 2`, Etc/UTC — offset from the fbi_cde day-3 slot) +
`secrets = { SIG_DATA_GOV_KEY = "sig-data-gov-key" }`. `runner.py`:
`congress_gov → accountability` map + `congress`/`page_offset` on
`document_outcomes`.

## Deterministic gate

- `tests/connectors/test_congress_gov_sweep.py` (23 tests): the REAL
  250-bill 2026-09-18 page-1 capture (committed fixture) + a synthetic
  FISA page — plan bounds (per_page ≤ 250, congresses=[119], ≤96 pages),
  vocabulary coverage of every ticket-named federal term, bounded
  `discover_more` expansion (count 18,887 → 75 pages; count 99,999 →
  capped at bound−1; a generated page never re-expands; drift loud),
  typed claims (conventional-citation typed identifier + verbatim raw,
  chamber, congress-as-session, federal jurisdiction, verbatim
  latest-action status, byte-range-into-title keyword locators, derived
  congress.gov public URL), never a `LegalInstrument`, `index_only`
  fallback, the real page → 250 index links + honest `empty` outcome +
  `truncated` flag, `bill_query` outcome row fields, fail-closed error
  envelope + malformed + non-bills payloads, no volatile claim fields,
  digest stability.
- `test_credential_transport.py`: `congress_gov` added — key rides
  `X-Api-Key`, never the URL; keyless sends no header.
- `test_review_status.py` / `test_source_registry.py`: counts
  (187 registered / 66 loadable / `_FLIPPED_SUBSET` +congress_gov).
- `make check` green: lint, format, mypy (231 files), **3302 passed**,
  verify-gen.

- Cloud Build `2329e6df` → `sig-api@sha256:de76f1e1…` (linux/amd64 via

- Secret IAM: `sig-data-gov-key` had NO bindings (the fbi_cde job runs on
